Out-of-fold cross-validated predictions (no model is stored)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Computes out-of-fold cross-validated predictions for a training table without persisting any model. Each row is predicted by a model trained on the other folds (`cv :=` folds, default 5), so the result is an honest, leakage-free prediction per row — ideal for building a held-out prediction column to score with metrics or to stack. Name the label with `target :=`, pick the `estimator :=`, optionally carry an `id :=` through, and tune via JSON `params :=`. Classification labels of any dtype are decoded back to the original values.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated out-of-fold predictions** — no model is stored.

- Each row is predicted by a model fit on the *other* folds (`cv :=`, default 5)
- `estimator :=`, `target :=`, optional `id :=` passthrough, JSON `params :=`
- Returns one `prediction` per input row (label or value), leakage-free

Use it to make a held-out prediction column for metrics or model stacking.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Out-of-fold confusion matrix on iris with species names: 5-fold cross_val_predict joined back to iris for the true and the predicted species (setosa is never confused; versicolor and virginica are mixed up a handful of times)", "sql": "SELECT a.target_name AS actual, l.target_name AS predicted, count(*) AS n FROM lightgbm.main.cross_val_predict((SELECT * EXCLUDE (target_name) FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), estimator := 'lgbm_classifier', target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', cv := 5) p JOIN lightgbm.main.iris() a USING (sample_id) JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT target, target_name FROM lightgbm.main.iris()) l ON l.target = p.prediction GROUP BY actual, predicted ORDER BY actual, predicted"}, {"description": "Distribution of the 5-fold out-of-fold predictions on iris", "sql": "SELECT prediction, count(*) AS n FROM lightgbm.main.cross_val_predict((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), estimator := 'lgbm_classifier', target := 'target') GROUP BY prediction ORDER BY prediction"}]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
One row per input row. The `prediction` column's type follows the label dtype (classification decodes back to the original labels; regression is `DOUBLE`), and naming `id :=` carries that input column through as the first column (the table below shows the common `sample_id` case).

#### Classification with integer or boolean labels

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prediction` | BIGINT | Out-of-fold predicted class label, decoded to the original label value. |

#### Classification with string labels

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prediction` | VARCHAR | Out-of-fold predicted class label, decoded to the original label value. |

#### Regression

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prediction` | DOUBLE | Out-of-fold predicted value. |

#### `id := '<column>'` passthrough

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sample_id` | INTEGER | The named id column, carried through as the first column. |

Per-fold cross-validation scores (accuracy or R^2); no model is stored

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Runs k-fold cross-validation and returns the held-out score for each fold (one `(fold, score, metric)` row), without storing any model. Name the label with `target :=`, choose the `estimator :=`, set the number of folds with `cv :=` (default 5), and tune via JSON `params :=`. The metric is the estimator's own scorer — accuracy for classifiers, R^2 for regressors. Aggregate the rows (e.g. `avg(score)`) for a single cross-validated performance estimate or to compare estimators/hyperparameters.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated fold scores** — one row per fold, no model stored.

- `estimator :=`, `target :=`, `cv :=` folds (default 5), JSON `params :=`
- Returns `(fold, score, metric)` — the held-out score for each fold

Scorer is the estimator's own (accuracy / R^2). Take `avg(score)` for a single cross-validated estimate.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "5-fold accuracy scores on iris", "sql": "SELECT fold, score FROM lightgbm.main.cross_val_score((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), estimator := 'lgbm_classifier', target := 'target', cv := 5)"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "fold", "type": "INTEGER", "description": "0-based fold index."}, {"name": "score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Held-out score for the fold (accuracy or R^2)."}, {"name": "metric", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "accuracy (classification) or r2 (regression)."}]

Delete a model from the registry

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Deletes a model from the registry by name (`drop_model('my_model')`) and returns one row `(model_name, dropped)` where `dropped` is true when a model was removed and false when the name did not exist. Idempotent and safe to call on an absent model. Use it to clean up models created by `fit`/`fit_lgbm_<task>`/search with a `model_name`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Delete a stored model** — registry cleanup.

- Call positionally: `drop_model('my_model')`
- Returns `(model_name, dropped)`; `dropped` is false if the name did not exist

Idempotent — safe on a missing model.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Delete a model by name; `dropped` is false when the name did not exist", "sql": "SELECT model_name, dropped FROM lightgbm.main.drop_model('no_such_model')"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "model_name", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Name of the model."}, {"name": "dropped", "type": "BOOLEAN", "description": "True if a model was deleted, False if it did not exist."}]

rows: Per-row SHAP feature contributions, long format (row, [class], feature, shap_value, base_value)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Streams a table through a stored model and emits SHAP-style per-row prediction contributions (LightGBM's `pred_contrib`) in long format: one row per (input row, feature) with `feature`, `shap_value` (how much that feature pushed this row's raw margin away from the model's base), and `base_value` (the expected margin). Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=` (a `BLOB`); name an `id :=` to tag every emitted row. For multiclass models an extra `class` column appears (one row per (row, class, feature)). Sum `shap_value` over a row's features and add `base_value` to recover the raw margin. Use it for local, per-prediction explanations.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**SHAP explanations** — per-row feature contributions, long format.

- Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`; optional `id :=` passthrough
- One row per (input row, feature): `feature`, `shap_value`, `base_value`
- Multiclass adds a `class` `BIGINT` column (one row per (row, class, feature))

`sum(shap_value) + base_value` = the row's raw margin. Local, per-prediction explanation.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Rank features by mean absolute SHAP contribution for a stored regressor 'diab_reg'", "sql": "SELECT feature, round(avg(abs(shap_value)), 4) AS mean_abs_shap FROM lightgbm.main.explain((SELECT * FROM lightgbm.main.diabetes()), model_name := 'diab_reg', id := 'sample_id') GROUP BY feature ORDER BY mean_abs_shap DESC"}, {"description": "Which features push each flower toward its own species? Join SHAP contributions from the stored 'iris_clf' to iris on sample and true class, then average |SHAP| per species and feature (petal length leads for all three species)", "sql": "SELECT i.target_name, e.feature, round(avg(abs(e.shap_value)), 3) AS mean_abs_shap FROM lightgbm.main.explain((SELECT * EXCLUDE (target_name) FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), model_name := 'iris_clf', id := 'sample_id') e JOIN lightgbm.main.iris() i ON i.sample_id = e.sample_id AND i.target = e.class GROUP BY i.target_name, e.feature ORDER BY i.target_name, mean_abs_shap DESC"}]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
Long format: one row per (input row, feature). Naming `id :=` carries that input column through as the first column (the table below shows the common `sample_id` case), and a multiclass model adds a `class` column so there is one row per (input row, class, feature).

#### Always present

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature` | VARCHAR | Feature column name. |
| `shap_value` | DOUBLE | Contribution of the feature to the raw margin. |
| `base_value` | DOUBLE | Model base (expected) raw-margin value. |

#### Multiclass models only

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `class` | BIGINT | Class index the contribution belongs to (0-based). |

#### `id := '<column>'` passthrough

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sample_id` | INTEGER | The named id column, carried through as the first column. |

Per-feature importance (split or gain) for a model, ranked

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Returns the booster's built-in per-feature importance for a stored model, one ranked row per feature (`feature`, `importance`, `rank`; rank 1 = most important, already sorted descending). Identify the model positionally by name (`feature_importance('m')`) or with `model :=` (a `BLOB`). Choose the `importance_type :=` — `gain` (default; total gain of the feature's splits) or `split` (the number of times the feature is used in a split). Features never used in a split report importance 0. A fast, model-native ranking; for a model-agnostic alternative use `permutation_importance`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Booster feature importance** — model-native, ranked.

- Identify the model by name (`feature_importance('m')`) or `model :=` `BLOB`
- `importance_type :=` `gain` (default; total split gain) | `split` (split count)
- Returns `(feature, importance, rank)`, sorted by importance descending

Unused features score 0. See `permutation_importance` for a model-agnostic measure.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Gain-based feature importance for a stored model", "sql": "SELECT feature, round(importance, 3) AS importance FROM lightgbm.main.feature_importance('iris_clf', importance_type := 'gain') WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank"}, {"description": "Do split-gain and permutation importance agree? Join the stored 'iris_clf' model's gain ranking to its permutation (accuracy-drop) ranking per feature; both put the two petal measurements first", "sql": "SELECT f.feature, f.rank AS gain_rank, p.rank AS permutation_rank, round(f.importance, 1) AS gain, round(p.importance_mean, 4) AS accuracy_drop FROM lightgbm.main.feature_importance('iris_clf', importance_type := 'gain') f JOIN lightgbm.main.permutation_importance((SELECT * EXCLUDE (target_name) FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), model_name := 'iris_clf', target := 'target', random_state := 42) p USING (feature) ORDER BY f.rank"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "feature", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "Feature column name."}, {"name": "importance", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Importance score for the chosen importance_type."}, {"name": "rank", "type": "INTEGER", "description": "1-based rank by importance (1 = most important)."}]
rows.vgi.title: Feature Importance

rows: SELECT feature, round(importance, 3) AS importance FROM lightgbm.main.feature_importance('iris_clf', importance_type := 'gain') WHERE rank <= 5 ORDER BY rank

SELECT f.feature, f.rank AS gain_rank, p.rank AS permutation_rank, round(f.importance, 1) AS gain, round(p.importance_mean, 4) AS accuracy_drop FROM lightgbm.main.feature_importance('iris_clf', importance_type := 'gain') f JOIN lightgbm.main.permutation_importance((SELECT * EXCLUDE (target_name) FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), model_name := 'iris_clf', target := 'target', random_state := 42) p USING (feature) ORDER BY f.rank
Fit a LightGBM estimator; returns the model as a `BLOB` and stores it when model_name is given

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Buffers a training table, fits a LightGBM estimator (`estimator :=` one of `lgbm_classifier` or `lgbm_regressor`), and returns a one-row training summary whose `model` column is a self-contained `BLOB` (booster text + metadata). Name the label column with `target :=`; every other column except an optional `id :=` passthrough becomes a feature — string columns are used as LightGBM's native categorical features and NULLs are kept as missing values. Hyperparameters go in a JSON `params :=` string. Pass `model_name :=` to also persist the model to the registry; otherwise it lives only in the returned `BLOB`. Feed that `BLOB` to `predict`/`explain`/`feature_importance` via `SET VARIABLE` + `getvariable()`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Fit a LightGBM model** — train and return a reusable model `BLOB`.

- Input: a training table `(SELECT ...)`; name the label with `target :=`, optionally an `id :=` passthrough
- `estimator :=` `lgbm_classifier` | `lgbm_regressor`; hyperparameters via JSON `params :=`
- Returns one row: `estimator`, `task`, `n_samples`/`n_features`/`n_classes`/`n_categorical`, `train_score`, `features`, and the `model` `BLOB`
- `model_name :=` also persists to the registry; string features are learned as native categoricals and classification labels of any dtype are decoded back on predict

Cross-validated grid search; returns the leaderboard + refit best model `BLOB` on the best row

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Runs an exhaustive cross-validated grid search over a LightGBM estimator's hyperparameters and returns the leaderboard — one row per combination tried, with its `params` (JSON), `mean_score`, `std_score`, `rank` (1 = best), and `metric` (accuracy or r2). Pick the estimator with `estimator := 'lgbm_classifier'` or `'lgbm_regressor'`, then give each hyperparameter you want swept its own list of candidate values (`num_leaves := [15, 31]`, `learning_rate := [0.05, 0.1]`, `n_estimators := [100, 300]`, ...); anything you leave out stays at the estimator default. Set `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, optional `id :=`. The refit best model rides as a `model` `BLOB` on the single best row — grab it with `WHERE model IS NOT NULL`.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated grid search** — exhaustive hyperparameter sweep.

- `estimator := 'lgbm_classifier'` | `'lgbm_regressor'`, then one list per swept hyperparameter (`num_leaves := [15, 31]`, `learning_rate := [0.05, 0.1]`, ...)
- `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, optional `id :=`
- Returns the leaderboard: `params`, `mean_score`, `std_score`, `rank`, `metric`

The refit best model is a `model` `BLOB` on the best row — `WHERE model IS NOT NULL`.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Grid-search num_leaves x learning_rate on iris", "sql": "SELECT params, mean_score, rank FROM lightgbm.main.grid_search((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', cv := 2, estimator := 'lgbm_classifier', num_leaves := [15, 31], learning_rate := [0.1]) ORDER BY rank"}]

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Table function that synthesises a random n-class classification problem (scikit-learn's `make_classification`). Control the shape with `n_samples`, `n_features`, `n_informative`, `n_classes`, and `random_state`; the output schema has a `sample_id`, one `feature_<i>` `DOUBLE` column per feature, and an integer `target`. rows.vgi.doc_md:

- `sample_id` `INTEGER`, `target` `INTEGER` (0-based label)
- one `feature_<i>` `DOUBLE` column per feature (width set by `n_features`)

| Name | Type | Description |

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature_0` | DOUBLE | First generated feature value. |
| `feature_1` | DOUBLE | Second generated feature value. |
| `feature_2` | DOUBLE | Third generated feature value. |

How a stored model's average prediction changes as one feature varies over a grid

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Computes the partial-dependence curve for one numeric feature: sweeps `feature :=` over a grid of `grid_resolution :=` points and reports the model's average prediction at each value, holding the rest of the buffered background table fixed. Returns `(feature_value, class, partial_dependence)` ordered along the grid; `class` is NULL for regression and the single binary curve, and is the class index (one curve per class) for multiclass. Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`. Numeric features only (categorical features raise a clear error). Use it to see the marginal effect and shape of a feature on the prediction.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Partial dependence** — marginal effect of one feature.

- `feature :=` (numeric only) swept over `grid_resolution :=` points
- Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`; input is the background table
- Returns `(feature_value, class, partial_dependence)` along the grid

`class` is NULL for regression/binary, the class index for multiclass (one curve each).
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Partial dependence of 'iris_clf' on petal length", "sql": "SELECT feature_value, round(partial_dependence, 4) AS pd FROM lightgbm.main.partial_dependence((SELECT * EXCLUDE (target_name) FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), model_name := 'iris_clf', feature := 'petal_length_cm', grid_resolution := 5) WHERE class = 0 ORDER BY feature_value"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "feature_value", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Value the feature was set to."}, {"name": "class", "type": "BIGINT", "description": "Class label (NULL for regression / the single binary curve)."}, {"name": "partial_dependence", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Average model output at this feature value."}]

Model-agnostic feature importance: the drop in score when each feature is shuffled, ranked

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Computes model-agnostic permutation importance over an evaluation table: for each feature, shuffle its values `n_repeats :=` times and measure the resulting drop in the model's score; a larger drop means a more important feature. Returns one ranked row per feature (`feature`, `importance_mean`, `importance_std`, `rank`; rank 1 = most important). Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`, name the held-out `target :=` column, and optionally set `scoring :=` and `random_state :=`. Unlike `feature_importance` this measures impact on real predictions and respects feature correlations, but it needs labelled data and is slower.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Permutation importance** — model-agnostic, ranked.

- Identify the model with `model_name :=` or `model :=`; name the `target :=` column
- `n_repeats :=` shuffles per feature, optional `scoring :=`, `random_state :=`
- Returns `(feature, importance_mean, importance_std, rank)`, sorted descending

Measures impact on real predictions (needs labels; slower than `feature_importance`).

Score a table through a stored model (model_name) or an inline model BLOB

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Streams a table through an already-fit LightGBM model and emits its predictions. Identify the model with either `model_name :=` (a registry name) or `model :=` (a `BLOB` from `fit`, passed via `SET VARIABLE` + `getvariable()` since a table function has only one subquery slot). Features are matched by name (order-independent; extra columns ignored; missing ones error at bind), and string/categorical columns are re-encoded exactly as at fit. The default output is the decoded `prediction` (the original label dtype for classifiers, value for regressors); the mutually exclusive modes `with_proba`, `output_margin`, and `pred_leaf` switch to per-class probabilities, the raw margin, or per-tree leaf indices respectively. Name an `id :=` column to carry it through.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Predict with a stored model** — score a table row by row.

- Identify the model with `model_name :=` *or* `model :=` (a `fit` `BLOB`)
- Features aligned by name; an optional `id :=` is carried through
- Default output: `prediction` (label or value)
- `with_proba := true` → one `proba_<label>` column per class; `output_margin := true` → a `margin` `DOUBLE`; `pred_leaf := true` → a `leaf` `INTEGER[]` (one index per tree) — the three modes are mutually exclusive
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Predict with the stored 'iris_clf' model", "sql": "SELECT sample_id, prediction FROM lightgbm.main.predict((SELECT * FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), model_name := 'iris_clf', id := 'sample_id') ORDER BY sample_id LIMIT 10"}]
rows.vgi.result_dynamic_columns_md:
The result shape depends on the prediction mode and on whether an `id` column is named. When `id :=` is given, that input column is carried through unchanged as the first column (the table below shows the common `sample_id` case). The prediction column itself is one of the mutually exclusive variants below: the default `prediction` (typed from the label dtype), `with_proba := true` (one `proba_<label>` column per class, classifiers only), `output_margin := true` (`margin`), or `pred_leaf := true` (`leaf`).

#### Default — classification with integer or boolean labels

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prediction` | BIGINT | Predicted class label, decoded to the original label value. |

#### Default — classification with string labels

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prediction` | VARCHAR | Predicted class label, decoded to the original label value. |

#### Default — regression

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prediction` | DOUBLE | Predicted value. |

#### `with_proba := true` (classifiers only)

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proba_<label>` | DOUBLE | Predicted probability of that class; one column per class, keyed by the original label. |

#### `output_margin := true`

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `margin` | DOUBLE | Raw (pre-link) margin score from the booster. |

#### `pred_leaf := true`

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `leaf` | INTEGER[] | Leaf index reached in each tree, one element per tree. |

#### `id := '<column>'` passthrough

| Name | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sample_id` | INTEGER | The named id column, carried through as the first column. |

Cross-validated randomized search: sample n_iter hyperparameter combinations

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Runs a cross-validated randomized search over a LightGBM estimator, sampling `n_iter :=` random hyperparameter combinations (capped at the grid size) instead of exhausting the grid — cheaper than `grid_search` for large spaces. Same arguments: `estimator :=` names the estimator and each swept hyperparameter takes a list of candidate values; omitted params stay at their default. Set `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, `search_seed :=` for reproducible sampling, optional `id :=`. Returns the same leaderboard (`params`, `mean_score`, `std_score`, `rank`, `metric`) with the refit best model as a `model` `BLOB` on the best row (`WHERE model IS NOT NULL`).
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Cross-validated randomized search** — sample the hyperparameter space.

- `estimator := 'lgbm_classifier'` | `'lgbm_regressor'`, then one list per swept hyperparameter
- `n_iter :=` combinations to sample (capped at grid size), `search_seed :=` for reproducibility
- `target :=`, `cv :=` folds, optional `id :=`

Cheaper than `grid_search` on large grids; best model is a `model` `BLOB` on the best row.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "Randomized-search num_leaves x learning_rate on iris", "sql": "SELECT params, mean_score, rank FROM lightgbm.main.randomized_search((SELECT sample_id, sepal_length_cm, sepal_width_cm, petal_length_cm, petal_width_cm, target FROM lightgbm.main.iris()), target := 'target', id := 'sample_id', n_iter := 2, cv := 2, estimator := 'lgbm_classifier', num_leaves := [15, 31, 63], learning_rate := [0.05, 0.1, 0.2]) ORDER BY rank"}]
rows.vgi.result_columns_schema: [{"name": "params", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "JSON of this combination's hyperparameters."}, {"name": "mean_score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Mean held-out CV score (accuracy or R^2)."}, {"name": "std_score", "type": "DOUBLE", "description": "Std-dev of the held-out CV scores."}, {"name": "rank", "type": "INTEGER", "description": "1-based rank by mean_score (1 = best)."}, {"name": "metric", "type": "VARCHAR", "description": "accuracy (classification) or r2 (regression)."}, {"name": "model", "type": "BLOB", "description": "Refit best model as a `BLOB` (non-NULL only on the best row)."}]

Wine recognition dataset (178 samples, 13 features, 3 classes)

rows.vgi.doc_llm: Zero-argument table function returning the wine-recognition dataset: 178 rows, one per wine sample, with 13 numeric chemical-analysis features (alcohol, malic acid, ash, magnesium, total phenols, flavanoids, colour intensity, hue, proline, ...), an integer `target` (0/1/2), the cultivar `target_name`, and a `sample_id`. A balanced 3-class dataset over continuous features — handy for multiclass classification demos.
rows.vgi.doc_md:
**Wine dataset** — 178 wines from three cultivars.

- `sample_id` `INTEGER` — 0-based row index
- 13 `DOUBLE` chemical features (alcohol, phenols, colour intensity, proline, ...)
- `target` `INTEGER` (0–2) and `target_name` the cultivar

Takes no arguments. A continuous-feature 3-class classification benchmark.
rows.vgi.example_queries: [{"description": "The ten strongest wines with their cultivar", "sql": "SELECT sample_id, alcohol, flavanoids, target_name FROM lightgbm.main.wine() WHERE alcohol > 13.5 ORDER BY alcohol DESC LIMIT 10"}]
